diseases.name: Common Cold
self_care: Rest and sleep well
Drink warm fluids (water, soup, herbal tea)
Steam inhalation twice daily
Salt-water gargle for throat pain
Keep room humidified
diseases.description: A viral infection of the upper respiratory tract causing nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat and mild cough. Resolves on its own in about a week.

diseases.name: Influenza (Flu)
self_care: Bed rest for the first 3-5 days
High fluid intake (2.5-3 L/day)
Antipyretic for fever
Isolate to avoid spreading
Monitor temperature twice daily
diseases.description: Influenza virus infection with abrupt high fever, severe body aches and marked fatigue. More intense than a common cold.
when_to_see_doctor: Fever above 40C or lasting over 5 days

diseases.name: COVID-19
self_care: Isolate and rest
Monitor oxygen saturation if pulse oximeter available
Hydrate well
Prone positioning if breathless
Seek urgent care if oxygen below 94%
diseases.description: SARS-CoV-2 infection with fever, cough, and characteristic loss of smell or taste. Breathlessness signals more serious disease.
when_to_see_doctor: Confusion or inability to stay awake

diseases.name: Acute Bronchitis
self_care: Warm fluids and steam inhalation
Avoid smoke and cold air
Honey with warm water for cough
Rest the voice
diseases.description: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes, usually after a cold, producing a persistent cough with phlegm lasting 2-3 weeks.

diseases.name: Pneumonia
self_care: Urgent medical review required
Rest and high fluid intake until seen
Do not delay antibiotics if prescribed
diseases.description: Infection of the lung air sacs causing fever, productive cough and breathlessness. Requires medical assessment and usually antibiotics.

diseases.name: Asthma Exacerbation
self_care: Use prescribed reliever inhaler as directed
Sit upright, stay calm, breathe slowly
Avoid triggers (dust, smoke, cold air)
Follow a written asthma action plan
diseases.description: Reversible narrowing of the airways causing wheeze, cough and breathlessness, often triggered by allergens, cold or exercise.

diseases.name: Allergic Rhinitis / Hay Fever
self_care: Identify and avoid allergens (pollen, dust mites, pet dander)
Rinse nose with saline
Keep windows closed during high pollen
Shower after outdoor exposure
diseases.description: Allergic inflammation of the nose and eyes triggered by airborne allergens, causing sneezing, itching and watery discharge.
when_to_see_doctor: Symptoms interfere with sleep or work

diseases.name: Acute Sinusitis
self_care: Steam inhalation 2-3 times daily
Saline nasal irrigation
Warm compress over the sinuses
Sleep with head elevated
diseases.description: Inflammation of the paranasal sinuses with facial pressure, blocked nose and headache, often following a cold.
when_to_see_doctor: Severe facial pain or swelling around the eye

diseases.name: Acute Gastroenteritis
self_care: Oral rehydration solution after every loose stool
Small frequent sips of fluid
Bland diet (rice, banana, toast)
Avoid dairy and oily food until better
diseases.description: Infection of the gut causing diarrhoea, vomiting and cramps, usually viral or food-borne. Main risk is dehydration.
when_to_see_doctor: Signs of dehydration (no urine, sunken eyes)
Symptoms over 5 days or in infants/elderly

diseases.name: Gastro-oesophageal Reflux (GERD)
self_care: Avoid spicy, oily and acidic food
Do not lie down for 3 hours after eating
Elevate the head of the bed
Eat smaller, more frequent meals
Reduce caffeine and alcohol
diseases.description: Stomach acid flowing back into the oesophagus causing burning chest discomfort, worse after meals or lying down.
when_to_see_doctor: Chest pain with breathlessness (rule out cardiac cause)

diseases.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
self_care: Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol
Stop smoking
Eat regular small meals
Avoid late-night eating
diseases.description: An open sore in the stomach or duodenal lining causing gnawing upper abdominal pain, often related to meals.
when_to_see_doctor: Vomiting blood or black tarry stool

diseases.name: Constipation
self_care: Increase dietary fibre (fruit, vegetables, whole grains)
Drink 2-3 L water daily
Daily walking or exercise
Do not ignore the urge to go
Establish a regular toilet routine
diseases.description: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements, usually due to low fibre, low fluid intake or inactivity.

diseases.name: Migraine
self_care: Rest in a dark, quiet room
Cold compress on the forehead
Stay hydrated
Identify and avoid triggers (sleep loss, certain foods, stress)
Keep a headache diary
diseases.description: Recurrent throbbing headache, often one-sided, with nausea and sensitivity to light and sound.
when_to_see_doctor: Headache with fever and stiff neck
New weakness, numbness or speech difficulty

diseases.name: Tension Headache
self_care: Neck and shoulder stretches
Regular sleep schedule
Reduce screen time and take breaks
Stress management and relaxation
Hydration
diseases.description: A band-like pressure headache on both sides, driven by stress, poor posture or muscle tension.
when_to_see_doctor: Headaches more than 15 days a month

diseases.name: Meningitis (suspected)
self_care: EMERGENCY — go to the nearest emergency department immediately
Do not wait for symptoms to settle
Call emergency services if unable to travel
diseases.description: Life-threatening infection of the membranes around the brain. Fever, severe headache, stiff neck and rash require immediate emergency care.
when_to_see_doctor: Immediately — this is a medical emergency

diseases.name: Stroke (suspected)
self_care: EMERGENCY — call emergency services immediately
Note the time symptoms started
Do not give food or drink
Do not drive yourself
diseases.description: Sudden loss of blood flow to part of the brain. Face droop, arm weakness and slurred speech need emergency treatment within minutes.
when_to_see_doctor: Arm or leg weakness on one side

diseases.name: Type 2 Diabetes (uncontrolled)
self_care: Structured meal plan, low refined sugar
30 minutes of activity 5 days a week
Daily foot checks
Home glucose monitoring as advised
Weight management
diseases.description: Chronic high blood sugar causing thirst, frequent urination, fatigue and slow healing. Needs medical confirmation and long-term management.
when_to_see_doctor: Always — confirm with blood glucose testing

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism
self_care: Take thyroid medication on an empty stomach
Regular thyroid function blood tests
Balanced diet with adequate iodine
Regular gentle exercise
Adequate sleep
diseases.description: Underactive thyroid causing fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain and low mood. Diagnosed by blood tests and treated with replacement hormone.

diseases.name: Hyperthyroidism
self_care: Limit caffeine
Adequate calorie and calcium intake
Regular thyroid monitoring
Stress reduction
diseases.description: Overactive thyroid causing heat intolerance, weight loss, anxiety and palpitations. Requires thyroid function testing.

diseases.name: Iron-Deficiency Anaemia
self_care: Iron-rich diet (red meat, lentils, spinach, fortified cereals)
Take iron with vitamin C to improve absorption
Avoid tea or coffee with iron-rich meals
Treat underlying cause of blood loss
diseases.description: Low red blood cell count from iron deficiency causing fatigue, breathlessness and pallor. Confirmed with a blood test.

diseases.name: Hypertension
self_care: Reduce salt to under 5 g/day
Regular aerobic exercise 30 min/day
Weight reduction
Limit alcohol and stop smoking
Home blood pressure monitoring
diseases.description: Persistently raised blood pressure, usually symptomless but damaging to heart, brain and kidneys over time.
when_to_see_doctor: Chest pain, breathlessness or severe headache

diseases.name: Angina / Cardiac Chest Pain
self_care: EMERGENCY if chest pain lasts over 15 minutes, is crushing, or spreads to arm/jaw — call emergency services
Stop activity and sit down
Chew aspirin only if advised by emergency services and not allergic
Do not drive yourself
diseases.description: Reduced blood flow to the heart muscle causing chest pressure on exertion. Unstable or prolonged pain is a heart attack emergency.
when_to_see_doctor: Immediately for new, severe or prolonged chest pain
Sweating with nausea and chest pain
Pain spreading to arm, neck or jaw

diseases.name: Heart Failure (decompensated)
self_care: Urgent medical review
Daily weight monitoring
Fluid and salt restriction as advised
Sleep propped up
Report rapid weight gain
diseases.description: The heart cannot pump enough blood, causing breathlessness, ankle swelling and fatigue. Needs medical management.
when_to_see_doctor: Breathlessness at rest or lying flat

diseases.name: Urinary Tract Infection
self_care: Drink 2-3 L water daily
Do not hold urine
Urinate after intercourse
Warm compress on the lower abdomen
diseases.description: Bacterial infection of the bladder causing burning urination, urgency and frequency. Upper tract involvement causes fever and flank pain.

diseases.name: Kidney Stones (renal colic)
self_care: Drink 2.5-3 L water daily
Strain urine to catch the stone
Pain relief as advised
Reduce salt and oxalate-rich foods
diseases.description: A stone in the urinary tract causing severe waves of flank pain radiating to the groin, with blood in urine.

diseases.name: Osteoarthritis
self_care: Low-impact exercise (swimming, cycling)
Weight management to reduce joint load
Hot or cold packs
Physiotherapy and strengthening
Assistive devices if needed
diseases.description: Wear-and-tear of joint cartilage causing pain and stiffness, worse with activity and better with rest.
when_to_see_doctor: Pain not controlled by simple analgesia

diseases.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis (flare)
self_care: Gentle range-of-motion exercise
Joint protection techniques
Rest during flares
Regular rheumatology follow-up
diseases.description: Autoimmune inflammation of the joints causing symmetrical swelling and morning stiffness lasting over an hour.

diseases.name: Gout
self_care: Elevate and rest the joint
Cold compress
Avoid alcohol, red meat and shellfish
Drink 2-3 L water daily
diseases.description: Uric acid crystals in a joint causing sudden severe pain, redness and swelling, classically the big toe.
when_to_see_doctor: Fever with hot swollen joint (rule out infection)

diseases.name: Fibromyalgia
self_care: Graded exercise programme
Structured sleep routine
Relaxation and mindfulness
Pacing of activities
Warm baths
diseases.description: Chronic widespread pain with fatigue, poor sleep and cognitive fog, without joint inflammation.
when_to_see_doctor: Always — needs assessment to exclude other causes

diseases.name: Urticaria (Hives)
self_care: Identify and avoid triggers (foods, drugs, heat, stress)
Cool compresses
Avoid scratching and hot showers
Loose cotton clothing
diseases.description: Raised itchy welts on the skin from histamine release, often allergic, each lesion lasting under 24 hours.
when_to_see_doctor: Swelling of lips, tongue or throat — emergency
Lesions lasting over 24 hours with bruising

diseases.name: Eczema / Atopic Dermatitis
self_care: Moisturise at least twice daily
Lukewarm short baths with gentle soap-free cleanser
Avoid wool, fragrance and known irritants
Keep nails short to avoid scratching damage
diseases.description: Chronic itchy inflamed skin with dry patches and flares, driven by skin barrier dysfunction and allergy.
when_to_see_doctor: Signs of infection (pus, yellow crust, fever)
Not responding to moisturiser and mild steroid

diseases.name: Fungal Skin Infection (tinea)
self_care: Keep the area clean and dry
Do not share towels or clothing
Wash and dry skin folds carefully
Treat all affected areas and household contacts
diseases.description: Fungal infection of the skin causing a ring-shaped itchy scaly rash, commonly in warm moist areas.

diseases.name: Cellulitis / Infected Wound
self_care: Keep the area clean and covered
Elevate the affected limb
Mark the edge of redness to track spread
Do not squeeze or puncture
diseases.description: Bacterial infection of deep skin causing spreading redness, warmth, swelling and pain, sometimes with fever.
when_to_see_doctor: High fever or feeling very unwell

diseases.name: Minor Burn / Scald
self_care: Cool under running lukewarm water for 20 minutes
Do not apply ice, butter or toothpaste
Cover with a clean non-stick dressing
Do not burst blisters
Keep the burn clean
diseases.description: Heat injury to the skin. Small superficial burns heal with cooling and dressings; large or deep burns need emergency care.
when_to_see_doctor: Burn larger than the palm of the hand
Burn on face, hands, joints or genitals
Black, white or charred skin — emergency

diseases.name: Conjunctivitis (pink eye)
self_care: Cool compress on closed eyes
Clean discharge with boiled cooled water
Do not share towels or pillows
Remove contact lenses
Wash hands frequently
diseases.description: Inflammation of the eye surface causing redness, discharge and grittiness, usually viral or bacterial.
when_to_see_doctor: Severe eye pain or light sensitivity

diseases.name: Otitis Media (middle ear infection)
self_care: Warm compress over the ear
Keep the ear dry
Sleep with the affected ear up
Pain relief as needed
diseases.description: Infection behind the eardrum causing earache, reduced hearing and often fever, common in children.
when_to_see_doctor: Fluid or pus from the ear
Swelling or redness behind the ear

diseases.name: Depressive Episode
self_care: Keep a regular sleep and activity schedule
Daily physical activity, even a short walk
Stay connected with supportive people
Structure small achievable goals
Seek professional psychological support
diseases.description: Persistent low mood and loss of interest lasting at least two weeks, affecting sleep, appetite and energy.
when_to_see_doctor: Always — assessment and support are available
Any thoughts of self-harm — seek help immediately
Unable to work or care for yourself

diseases.name: Generalised Anxiety
self_care: Diaphragmatic breathing and grounding exercises
Limit caffeine and alcohol
Regular aerobic exercise
Structured worry time and journaling
Consider talking therapy
diseases.description: Excessive persistent worry with restlessness, poor sleep and physical tension, present most days for months.
when_to_see_doctor: Always if it affects daily life
Any thoughts of self-harm — immediate help
Physical symptoms needing exclusion of other causes

diseases.name: Dengue Fever
self_care: Rest and high fluid intake
Paracetamol only — avoid ibuprofen, aspirin and other NSAIDs
Monitor for warning signs
Daily platelet check if advised
diseases.description: Mosquito-borne viral infection causing high fever, severe bone and joint pain and a rash. Can progress to bleeding complications.
when_to_see_doctor: Warning signs: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums

diseases.name: Malaria
self_care: Urgent medical assessment and blood test required
High fluid intake
Paracetamol for fever
Do not self-treat with leftover antimalarials
diseases.description: Parasitic infection transmitted by mosquitoes causing cyclical fever with rigors and sweating. Needs urgent blood testing and treatment.
when_to_see_doctor: Always and urgently — needs a blood test

diseases.name: Typhoid Fever
self_care: Medical assessment and blood culture required
High fluid intake
Soft bland diet
Strict hand hygiene to avoid spreading
diseases.description: Bacterial infection from contaminated food or water causing a stepwise rising fever with abdominal pain and constipation.
when_to_see_doctor: Always — needs blood tests and antibiotics
Severe abdominal pain or blood in stool

diseases.name: Tonsillitis / Strep Throat
self_care: Warm salt-water gargles
Cool drinks and soft foods
Rest the voice
Paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain
Stay hydrated
diseases.description: Infection of the tonsils causing severe throat pain, difficulty swallowing, fever and tender neck glands.
when_to_see_doctor: Symptoms over 5 days or recurrent episodes

diseases.name: Anaphylaxis (severe allergic reaction)
diseases.description: Life-threatening whole-body allergic reaction with airway swelling, breathing difficulty and falling blood pressure. This is a medical emergency.
when_to_see_doctor: Use a prescribed adrenaline auto-injector without delay
Do not wait to see whether symptoms settle

diseases.name: Obstructive Sleep Apnoea
self_care: Sleep on your side rather than your back
Avoid alcohol and sedatives before bed
Keep a regular sleep and wake time
Lose weight if overweight
Raise the head of the bed slightly
diseases.description: Repeated collapse of the upper airway during sleep, causing loud snoring, pauses in breathing and unrefreshing sleep. Daytime sleepiness and morning headaches are typical.
when_to_see_doctor: Witnessed pauses in breathing during sleep
Falling asleep while driving or working

diseases.name: Vertigo (BPPV)
self_care: Move your head slowly and deliberately
Sit down immediately when the spinning starts
Sleep with your head slightly raised
Avoid sudden head turns and looking straight up
Rise slowly from lying to sitting to standing
diseases.description: Brief intense spinning brought on by changes in head position, caused by displaced crystals in the inner ear. Hearing is not usually affected.
when_to_see_doctor: Vertigo with new hearing loss or ringing
Double vision, slurred speech or weakness
Symptoms not settling after a week

diseases.name: Deep Vein Thrombosis (suspected)
self_care: Do not massage or rub the leg
Keep the leg still and elevated slightly
Do not apply heat to the area
Seek urgent medical assessment the same day
diseases.description: A clot in a deep vein, usually of the calf, causing one-sided pain, swelling and warmth. The danger is the clot travelling to the lungs, so this needs same-day assessment.
when_to_see_doctor: Any new one-sided calf pain or swelling
Recent surgery, immobility or long travel

diseases.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
self_care: Eat regular small meals rather than large ones
Keep a food and symptom diary to spot triggers
Reduce caffeine, alcohol and fizzy drinks
Try soluble fibre such as oats or ispaghula
Manage stress with relaxation or breathing exercises
diseases.description: A functional bowel disorder causing cramping, bloating and a change in bowel habit without structural disease. Symptoms come and go and are often stress-linked.

diseases.name: Haemorrhoids (Piles)
self_care: Increase fibre and water to soften stools
Avoid straining and prolonged sitting on the toilet
Take warm sitz baths for 10 minutes
Do not delay the urge to go to the toilet
Gentle wipe with moist tissue rather than dry paper
diseases.description: Swollen vascular cushions around the anus causing bright red bleeding and discomfort, usually related to straining or constipation.
when_to_see_doctor: Bleeding that is dark or mixed with stool
Weight loss or a change in bowel habit
Bleeding that continues beyond a week

diseases.name: Oral Candidiasis (thrush)
self_care: Rinse the mouth with salt water
Eat plain yoghurt or take probiotics
Avoid sugary food and drinks
Stop smoking
Keep dentures out at night and clean them
diseases.description: A fungal infection of the mouth causing white patches that can be scraped off, soreness and a bad taste. Common after antibiotics, inhalers or in diabetes.

diseases.name: Dental Abscess
self_care: Rinse with warm salt water
Avoid very hot, cold or sweet food
Sleep with the head slightly raised
Do not place aspirin directly on the gum
See a dentist as soon as possible
diseases.description: A collection of pus at the root of a tooth, causing severe throbbing pain, swelling of the gum or face and sometimes fever.
when_to_see_doctor: Swelling spreading to the eye or neck
Pain not controlled by regular painkillers

diseases.name: Otitis Externa (swimmer's ear)
self_care: Keep the ear canal completely dry
Do not insert cotton buds or fingers
Avoid swimming until healed
Use a warm compress for pain
Use ear plugs when showering
diseases.description: Infection of the ear canal causing pain that is worse when the outer ear is pulled, with itching and discharge. Often follows swimming or water exposure.
when_to_see_doctor: Severe pain or swelling around the ear
Diabetes or a weakened immune system

diseases.name: Peripheral Neuropathy
self_care: Inspect your feet daily for cuts or blisters
Wear well-fitting protective footwear
Keep blood sugar well controlled if diabetic
Avoid alcohol
Take care with hot water bottles and heaters
diseases.description: Damage to the peripheral nerves causing tingling, numbness or burning in the hands and feet, most often from diabetes or vitamin B12 deficiency.
when_to_see_doctor: Symptoms affecting only one side suddenly

diseases.name: Parkinson's Disease (suspected)
self_care: Keep physically active with walking and stretching
Do balance and coordination exercises
Use aids around the home to prevent falls
Keep a regular routine and sleep schedule
Ask about speech and physiotherapy referral
diseases.description: A progressive neurological condition causing a rest tremor, slowness of movement and stiffness. Diagnosis is clinical and needs specialist assessment.
when_to_see_doctor: Slowness or stiffness affecting daily tasks
Reduced facial expression or small handwriting

diseases.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
self_care: Aim for regular exercise most days
Choose lower-glycaemic, high-fibre foods
Lose 5-10% of body weight if overweight
Track your cycles to spot patterns
Discuss screening for diabetes and blood pressure
diseases.description: A hormonal condition with irregular or painful periods, excess androgens and often metabolic features such as insulin resistance. Needs clinical assessment and blood tests.
when_to_see_doctor: Periods more than 35 days apart or absent
Rapid hair growth on the face or body

diseases.name: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
self_care: Reduce fluid intake in the evening
Cut down caffeine and alcohol
Empty the bladder fully by taking your time
Avoid decongestant and antihistamine medicines
Keep active and maintain a healthy weight
diseases.description: Non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate causing a weak stream, hesitancy, urgency and needing to pass urine at night.
when_to_see_doctor: Fever with pain in the back or groin

diseases.name: Varicose Veins
self_care: Elevate the legs above heart level when resting
Avoid standing still for long periods
Use compression stockings if advised
Keep active with walking
Moisturise the skin over the veins
diseases.description: Enlarged twisted veins, usually in the legs, causing aching, heaviness and swelling that is worse at the end of the day.
when_to_see_doctor: Skin ulcer or bleeding from a vein
Redness, warmth and tenderness in the leg
Severe pain not relieved by elevation

diseases.name: Scabies
self_care: Treat all household members on the same day
Wash bedding, towels and clothing in hot water
Apply treatment to the whole body, not just itchy areas
Avoid close skin contact until treated
Trim nails to avoid skin damage from scratching
diseases.description: Infestation by the scabies mite causing intense itching that is worse at night, with a pimple-like rash often between the fingers and on the wrists.
when_to_see_doctor: Signs of skin infection such as pus or spreading redness
Itching in a baby or elderly person

diseases.name: Shingles (Herpes Zoster)
self_care: Keep the rash clean and dry
Do not burst the blisters
Wear loose cotton clothing over the area
Use a cool compress for pain
Avoid contact with pregnant women and newborns until crusted
diseases.description: Reactivation of chickenpox virus along a nerve, causing a painful band of blisters on one side of the body, often preceded by burning or tingling.
when_to_see_doctor: Rash near the eye or nose
Severe pain not controlled by painkillers
Weakness or difficulty moving a limb

diseases.name: Acne Vulgaris
self_care: Wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser
Do not squeeze or pick at spots
Use a non-comedogenic moisturiser and sunscreen
Avoid heavy oil-based cosmetics
Be patient - treatments take 6-8 weeks
diseases.description: Blocked and inflamed hair follicles on the face, chest and back producing blackheads, whiteheads and red spots. Common in adolescence and young adulthood.
when_to_see_doctor: No improvement after 8 weeks of treatment
Significant impact on mood or confidence

diseases.name: Psoriasis
self_care: Moisturise the skin generously every day
Get sensible sunlight exposure
Avoid scratching and picking at plaques
Reduce stress and alcohol
Stop smoking
diseases.description: A chronic immune condition producing well-defined red plaques with silvery scale, typically on the elbows, knees and scalp.
when_to_see_doctor: Joint pain and swelling with the rash

diseases.name: Heat Exhaustion
self_care: Move to a cool shaded place immediately
Lie down and raise the legs
Sip cool water or an oral rehydration solution
Loosen or remove excess clothing
Cool the skin with wet cloths and fanning
diseases.description: Overheating from prolonged heat exposure causing heavy sweating, weakness, dizziness and nausea. Body temperature is usually below 40C and the person remains conscious.
when_to_see_doctor: Hot dry skin with no sweating

diseases.name: Insomnia
self_care: Keep the same sleep and wake time every day
Get out of bed if awake for more than 20 minutes
Avoid screens and bright light for an hour before bed
No caffeine after midday and no alcohol at night
Keep the bedroom cool, dark and quiet
diseases.description: Difficulty falling or staying asleep with daytime consequences such as fatigue and poor concentration, on most nights for at least two weeks.
when_to_see_doctor: Loud snoring or witnessed breathing pauses
Sleep problems lasting more than a month

diseases.name: Panic Disorder
self_care: Learn slow breathing: in for 4, hold 4, out for 6
Stay where you are until the surge passes
Reduce caffeine and alcohol
Keep a diary of attacks and what preceded them
Get regular exercise and sleep
diseases.description: Recurrent unexpected surges of intense fear with a racing heart, breathlessness and a sense of doom, plus worry about the next attack.
when_to_see_doctor: Chest pain with sweating or pain spreading to the arm
Avoiding normal activities for fear of attacks

diseases.name: Mechanical Low Back Pain
self_care: Keep moving - avoid prolonged bed rest
Return to normal activity gradually
Use heat packs for muscle spasm
Set up your chair and screen properly
Lift with the knees, not the back
diseases.description: Pain in the lower back from muscles, ligaments or joints, often after strain or poor posture, without nerve involvement.
when_to_see_doctor: Numbness around the groin or buttocks
Difficulty passing urine or loss of control
Pain after a fall or with fever or weight loss

diseases.name: Sciatica
self_care: Keep active within the limits of the pain
Avoid heavy lifting and twisting
Use heat for muscle spasm
Try gentle stretching as pain settles
Set up a supportive chair and mattress
diseases.description: Pain radiating from the lower back down the leg along the path of the sciatic nerve, often with tingling or numbness, from nerve compression.

diseases.name: Menopausal Symptoms
self_care: Dress in layers and keep rooms cool
Reduce caffeine, alcohol and spicy food
Do regular weight-bearing exercise
Ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D
Use a water-based lubricant if needed
diseases.description: Symptoms around the menopause including hot flushes, night sweats, sleep disturbance and mood change, caused by falling oestrogen levels.
when_to_see_doctor: Any bleeding after 12 months without periods
Symptoms of low mood that persist

diseases.name: Vaginal Candidiasis (thrush)
self_care: Wear loose cotton underwear
Avoid perfumed soaps and douching
Keep the area clean and dry
Avoid tight synthetic clothing
Reduce sugary foods
diseases.description: A fungal infection causing thick white discharge, intense itching and soreness. Common after antibiotics or in diabetes.

diseases.name: Obesity / Overweight
self_care: Aim for 150 minutes of moderate activity a week
Reduce portion sizes and sugary drinks
Weigh yourself once a week at the same time
Target 5-10% body weight loss first - it already improves blood pressure and sugar
Keep a simple food and activity diary
diseases.description: Excess body fat that raises the risk of diabetes, high blood pressure, joint disease and sleep apnoea.
when_to_see_doctor: BMI 30 or above, or 27 with a related condition
Weight rising despite diet and exercise changes
Knee or hip pain limiting activity
